content: I'll read the test image to analyze the plant disease symptoms.

**Visual analysis:**

- **Plant part**: Sugarcane leaf (long, narrow, laid flat on white background)
- **Pattern**: Clear longitudinal stripes running parallel to the leaf veins — alternating bands of normal green and pale cream/yellow-white
- **Color**: Multiple stripes of varying widths in green and pale cream/yellowish-white
- **Texture/Distribution**: Uniform striping pattern across the full width of the leaf; no discrete spots, lesions, or focal damage

**Reasoning through candidate classes:**

- **Brown_Spot / Yellow_Spot**: Eliminated — no discrete circular/oval lesions present
- **Grassy_Shoot / Sett_Rot**: Eliminated — those affect plant architecture/setts, not leaf coloration
- **Yellow_Leaf**: Eliminated — Yellow Leaf causes yellowing concentrated along the midrib, not full-width parallel striping
- **Leaf_Scald**: Possible, but Leaf Scald typically shows 1–3 distinct scalded white stripes with water-soaked margins, not the multi-band mosaic seen here
- **Sugarcane_Mosaic_Virus**: Shows irregular mosaic/mottled patches; this pattern is more regularly striped
- **Streak_Mosaic_Scsmv**: The hallmark symptom is well-defined, longitudinal pale-yellow/cream streaks alternating with green bands running parallel to the veins — precisely what is visible here

The uniformly distributed, parallel, longitudinal alternating green and pale cream stripes are the classic signature of Sugarcane Streak Mosaic Virus (SCSMV).
